notes: PRIMARY IR data verified for FY2025 and Q1 2026. FY2025: sales EUR 44.05B (+4.0% LFL, +1.3% reported), operating profit EUR 8,891.9M, operating margin 20.2% (+20bps, record gross margin 74.3%), diluted EPS ex-non-recurring EUR 12.71 (+0.4%), reported EPS EUR 11.44, net cash flow EUR 7,161.6M (+7.8%), dividend EUR 7.20 proposed. Q1 2026: sales EUR 12.15B, +3.6% reported, +7.6% LFL (+6.7% adjusted ex-IT-transformation one-offs), FX -5.5%, perimeter +1.5% (Kering Beaute closed Mar 31, 2026 added ~1.5pp), constant-FX +9.1%; Q1 was sales-only release so no margin/EPS. fcf_margin computed 7.16/44.05=16.3%. ROIC ~13.5% per aggregators (GuruFocus 13.3%, some sources cite higher 18% on different methodology). SBC is ESTIMATED and structurally immaterial: L'Oreal is a French company paying mostly cash comp; historical share-based payment ~EUR 175-200M/yr (~0.4% of revenue, ~2.5% of FCF) - low dilution risk for R9; exact FY2025 figure not pulled from Universal Registration Document within timebox. Net cash position -EUR 2.05B (cash EUR 9.87B vs debt EUR 11.92B) per stockanalysis; converted to ~-USD 2.2B at EUR/USD ~1.08; ND/EBITDA -0.21x. Market cap EUR ~201.8B -> ~USD 218B at ~1.08. Forward P/E 27.18 (stockanalysis, Jun 22) vs ~35.7 5yr avg forward = ~24% discount; PEG 3.76. DROP CLASSIFICATION = not_depressed: stock only ~7% off 52w high and ~22% off May-2024 ATH, while Q1 2026 organic accelerated to +7.6% (beat, shares +8-9% on print) and FY2025 hit record margins. Valuation de-rated from COVID-era peak multiples (now ~24% below own 5yr fwd avg) but fundamentals are improving, not deteriorating - this is multiple normalization, not a fear-driven selloff of a broken business.
